title: Which details belong in a condition photograph of a fragile keepsake?
description: Show the whole keepsake and closer views of visible concerns or details that matter to the proposed arrangement.

sections.heading: Which details belong in a condition photograph of a fragile keepsake?
paragraphs: Show the whole keepsake and closer views of visible concerns or details that matter to the proposed arrangement. Date the photographs and describe only what you can observe, such as loose parts or curled edges. Avoid unnecessary handling or attempted repair. Keep irreplaceable originals with you until suitability and current transfer instructions are confirmed.

title: Should I describe the current condition of an item?

sections.heading: Should I describe the current condition of an item?
paragraphs: Yes. Record visible condition and any treatment or handling history you actually know. Distinguish your observations from information supplied by someone else. Clear photographs can support the discussion, but they do not establish a diagnosis or preservation suitability. Do not clean, alter or send an irreplaceable item based on a general reference image.

title: Can I supply photographs before handing anything over?
description: Photographs are an appropriate starting point for discussing what you would like to preserve and its condition.

sections.heading: Can I supply photographs before handing anything over?
paragraphs: Photographs are an appropriate starting point for discussing what you would like to preserve and its condition. Include a whole view and relevant details, with a simple item list. They do not guarantee that the material is suitable. Wait for the atelier's guidance and confirmed transfer arrangements before sending sentimental originals.

title: How can I explain which objects matter most?
description: Give each item a reference and explain its significance in a short, relevant note.

sections.heading: How can I explain which objects matter most?
paragraphs: Give each item a reference and explain its significance in a short, relevant note. Mark which items are essential to consider and which are optional. Match photographs to the list. You can explain meaning without sharing unnecessary personal history. Priority does not establish that an item can be preserved or included in the final design.

title: Can an arrangement reference guarantee the final appearance?

sections.heading: Can an arrangement reference guarantee the final appearance?
paragraphs: No. An arrangement reference shows a visual intention, not a guaranteed preservation outcome. Label illustrative or generated imagery and explain which relationships matter, such as orientation or spacing. The actual materials and their condition need assessment. Do not infer permanent colour, exact shape or suitability from a clear floral-block visualization.

title: Where do I ask about suitability for preservation?
description: Use the preservation or custom-piece brief to describe the materials, condition and intended idea, with clear photographs.

sections.heading: Where do I ask about suitability for preservation?
paragraphs: Use the preservation or custom-piece brief to describe the materials, condition and intended idea, with clear photographs. Ask specifically about suitability before making transfer arrangements. The current guidance says to keep sentimental originals until the atelier confirms suitability and provides instructions. A catalogue image cannot answer that question for your particular item.

title: Should I arrange transport before speaking with the atelier?
description: Wait until suitability and current transfer instructions are confirmed for the actual items.

sections.heading: Should I arrange transport before speaking with the atelier?
paragraphs: Wait until suitability and current transfer instructions are confirmed for the actual items. Check the recipient, destination and arrangements rather than relying on a general address or an old message. Keep a condition record and item list for the discussion. This answer does not prescribe packing or transport methods for fragile or irreplaceable materials.

title: Can personal names be kept out of a public project story?
description: Public use is a separate permission decision from a private design request.

sections.heading: Can personal names be kept out of a public project story?
paragraphs: Public use is a separate permission decision from a private design request. State which names, dates, images or story details must remain private and review any proposed public wording and photographs against that choice. Do not assume that personalization on an object authorizes the same information to appear in a website story.

title: What if family members have different preferences?
description: Collect the different priorities against the same item photographs and proposed arrangement.

sections.heading: What if family members have different preferences?
paragraphs: Collect the different priorities against the same item photographs and proposed arrangement. Identify shared preferences and unresolved choices, then agree who will communicate the consolidated brief. Do not imply consent from absent participants. Material suitability remains a separate question, even if the family agrees on the desired visual direction.

title: Where will the agreed preservation details be recorded?
description: Keep the confirmed details with the current agreed design and specification, including the item references, arrangement and any approved personalization.

sections.heading: Where will the agreed preservation details be recorded?
paragraphs: Keep the confirmed details with the current agreed design and specification, including the item references, arrangement and any approved personalization. Preserve earlier preferences as superseded notes rather than mixing them into the current version. A saved inquiry records the request; it does not itself confirm preservation suitability, the final design or production.
